thread:
alex_support: FYI — customer reported a 400 when calling pdf_extractor with metadata. They pasted payload from Notepad.
jen_customer: Hey, the toolcall keeps failing when I include author names like O'Connor and a Windows copy/paste. Error: 400 invalid_json. Full request below.
jen_customer: ```
POST /v1/tools/pdf_extractor/call
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "document_url": "https://s3.amazonaws.com/acme/report.pdf",
  "metadata": {
    "author": "O'Connor",
    "notes": "Copied from Word — may include weird chars",
  },
  "attachments": [
    {"name": "cover.jpg", "size": 23456,},
  ],
}
```
jen_customer: And response body was: `{"error":"invalid_json","message":"Unexpected token ',' at position 189"}`
alex_support: Thx. Can you paste the raw bytes or curl that reproduces it? Is this via our JS SDK or directly with curl/pwsh?
jen_customer: Using PowerShell on Windows, pasted JSON into a here-string and then curl. Repro is below.
jen_customer: ```powershell
$body = @"
{
  "document_url": "https://s3.amazonaws.com/acme/report.pdf",
  "metadata": {
    "author": "O'Connor",
    "notes": "From Word\r\n",
  },
  "attachments": [
    {"name": "cover.jpg", "size": 23456,},
  ],
}
"@
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tools/pdf_extractor/call -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d $body -v
```
priya_engineer: ugh — looks like two problems: trailing commas in the JSON (after notes and inside attachments), and Windows may have added a BOM at start from Notepad which some parsers choke on. Also the apostrophe in O'Connor should be fine if quoted with double quotes, but combined issues can confuse some validators.
sam_devex: If you pipe that through a strict JSON parser you should see the error. Quick check: `echo $body | python -m json.tool` (pwsh) or `jq .` will fail with position info.
priya_engineer: Repro locally — I copied the exact here-string and ran it in pwsh: parser fails with Unexpected token ',' at the position inside the array because of the extra trailing comma after the object. Also when I opened the file in Notepad the file had a U+FEFF at the start. Some server JSON libs (older Java ones) will treat the BOM as a stray char and then the trailing comma makes the rest invalid.
priya_engineer: Repro steps I used:```bash
# on windows pwsh, reproduce with same here-string
# 1) create body with the same here-string (Notepad paste -> save as UTF-8 with BOM)
# 2) curl as above
# server responds 400 invalid_json with same message
```
alex_support: Any immediate customer-facing fixes?
priya_engineer: Short-term: remove trailing commas and save the file as UTF-8 without BOM. In PowerShell you can do: `Set-Content -Path body.json -Value $body -Encoding utf8` (that writes without BOM). Or sanitize before sending: `$safe = $body -replace ',\s*([\]}])', '$1'` (quick hack to strip trailing commas). Better: build JSON with an object and use `ConvertTo-Json` or our SDK's JSON serializer — don't hand-edit strings.
sam_devex: Also added a diagnostic in our support tool: if we catch a JSON parse error, return a small hint 'looks like trailing comma or BOM' when the byte 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF appears. Will avoid the generic position-only message.
priya_engineer: Filed SDK bug and PR to Node SDK that was concatenating template pieces with an extra comma when attachments array length === 1. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-sdk/pull/142 (internal).
jen_customer: I patched the payload (removed trailing commas and re-sent with -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @body.json) — works now, thank you :thumbsup:
alex_support: Great. Closing for now but leaving the improved error hint and SDK fix in the backlog. If customer wants, we can add a small client-side sanitizer in the JS SDK to strip BOM and trailing commas before sending.
inc_bot: incident-1234 annotated — root cause: malformed client JSON (trailing commas + BOM). followup: push SDK patch to staging. :white_check_mark:
